chunks: In the book of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿImrān al-Ashʿarī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, who raises it to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
Regarding a man whom a matter grieves and who seeks a need.
He said: He should pray two rakʿahs and recite in one of them
a thousand times, and in the other once; then he asks for his need.

key_terms.الْحَاجَةَ: the need or request being sought
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, recited here as part of the prayer
key_terms.يَحْزُنُهُ: grieves him or causes him distress

ai.seo_question: What prayer should a person perform when distressed and seeking a need?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a salat for one who is distressed by a matter and seeks the fulfillment of a need. It instructs praying two rakʿahs, reciting Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ a thousand times in one rakʿah and once in the other, then asking Allah for the need.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1549 - In the book of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, narrated by Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, raised to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)
regarding a man troubled by a matter and in need of something,
Imam (as) said: "He should pray two rak'ahs and recite in one of them
a thousand times, and in the other rak'ah he should recite it once, then ask for his need."
